name: MD-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 10 points and Olszewski is an incumbent
Massive fundraising gap: $1.04M raised and $614K on hand vs. Wallace's $20K
Prediction markets price Democratic win at about 94%
No public polling in the race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Olszewski: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and an overwhelming money advantage over a barely funded challenger. Markets agree, pricing a Democratic win near certain, so the forecast stays at a Safe D with a margin in the low twenties.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much closer race or unexpected outside spending against Olszewski would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Johnny Olszewski, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking a second term in a Maryland district that favored Democrats by about ten points at the presidential level. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised over a million dollars and holding more than $600,000, while Republican Dave Wallace has raised roughly $20,000 and has little outside support.

No public polls cover the race, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at about 94 percent. With the incumbent well positioned and the challenger underfunded, the seat is rated Safe Democratic.
